risk_reasons: Restoring policy state can widen autonomy and must preserve confirmation, readiness, suspension and tenant authorization.
Refusal schema changes and fenced ledger writes affect durable tenant data.
goal: Owners can restore prior settings through reviewed proposals and see durable policy refusals as a distinct card and Restraint decision.
non_goals: Changing Run D's deployed candidate during its 24-hour observation
Model-authored restore state, direct settings mutation from a turn, or bundled owner Apply
A new refusal table, framework, provider, dependency or background scheduler
External Claude or Opus development/review delegates
user_visible_behavior: Every applied receipt offers Restore; it prepares a normal pending proposal labelled Restore, with fresh current-state versions and ordinary Apply friction.
Put it back how it was resolves restore_last server-side for the exact stated scope using the same preparation function.
clear_location_override is the eighth ordinary model-visible proposable, with full before/after, inherited policy consequences and suspension-aware execution.
A bounded paginated operating-rules timeline shows applied proposals in deterministic order beyond the latest 50 conversation turns.
The six policy-refusal reasons render server-owned rule wording without Apply, persist in fenced completion, reload under the distinct refused key, and appear as a ninth Restraint category.
invariants: Turn submission never applies settings or posts publicly; every restore is separately approved.
Restore inputs and provenance come only from a validated same-account applied Receipt; model and public settings schemas reject internal restore fields.
Apply retains account/business-before-proposal lock order, actor revalidation, opaque version comparison, expansion readiness and exact typed confirmation.
A restore of an existing one-field change writes only that field; an inverse of clear restores the exact prior row dials atomically, with one final-state exposure decision and audit.
Suspension state is never copied from historical input, deleted or cleared by restore; current suspension controls the result.
Refusal ledger writes use src/lib/refusals/write.ts only and commit or roll back with the winning fenced completion.
Refusal content lane requires business_id; policy lane requires null business_id; existing migration116 constraints remain valid for all old lanes.
The Restraint projection exposes stored category, timestamp and safe subject information only; no ledger reason columns, owner text or moderation prose leak.
Migration121 is local-only during D observation and is applied staging then production in one later approved window, verified by introspection.
E final review fork is normalized onto main after D and its closeout merge; no final E gate claim is made over the temporary stacked base.
edge_cases: Restore a null/default tone without admitting null to the ordinary model set_tone input.
Restore custom threshold/veto/cap after clearing an override, then undo that restore back to absence.
Restore original account-default absence using the existing clear_account_default semantics.
A suspended clear preserves the row and suspension and truthfully previews the resulting manual threshold.
A parent policy change between preparation and Apply makes a location restore stale.
Concurrent repeated Restore requests return one pending proposal for the same source and version; later state gets a freshly prepared proposal.
Foreign, unapplied, malformed, obsolete or missing source receipts fail without a write.
Each distinct refusal in the same lane gets its own server-minted subject ID; repeated identical references are rejected or deduplicated before persistence.
A lost turn fence persists neither refusal nor restore proposal; a ledger failure rolls the whole completion back.
The exact say we are licensed fixture is refused and never captured as unsupported.
